saves.reason: Recommended after V.V. Lightbody’s Period Piece (especially Practice Smiling) and Hannah Cohen’s Earthstar Mountain. Closest combined match: swirling woodwinds, syrupy bass, pizzicato strings, bongos and Latin rhythms; bright arrangements carrying insecurity and self-reassurance. Try My love is right, then Sur mes joues rosées. More French 1960s-pop and country touches than the anchors.

The colourful psych-pop branch of the V.V. Lightbody / Hannah Cohen lane: dulcet vocals, flute, harp, funky bass and warped synths, with small arrangement surprises. Try Pacific Ave, then Moon Canyon Park. More sugary, synthetic and retro-futurist than Period Piece or Earthstar Mountain.

For the gentle but irresistible groove shared by Period Piece and Earthstar Mountain: retro-soul, light psychedelia, breezy indie pop, understated jazzy guitars/keys and velvety, almost hypnotic bass and drums. Try Oas, then Vi smälter. Swedish-language vocals and fewer prominent orchestral/woodwind flourishes.

The lush orchestral-soul and complicated-feelings branch of the Hannah Cohen / V.V. Lightbody comparison. Airy singing, luxuriant Spacebomb strings and horns, sweetness tempered by heartbreak and strong grooves; OOR explicitly compares Cohen to Prass. Try Bird of Prey, then My Baby Don’t Understand Me. More dramatic and soul-oriented, less samba/psych.

A historical parallel to the Period Piece / Earthstar Mountain lane, not a verified direct influence: wispy intimate vocals, sophisticated jazz chords, orchestral sunshine-pop, understated funk, flute/oboe and psychedelic flourishes. Try Sunday Morning, then Love for the stranger flute-and-groove side. Vintage recording and sometimes sweeter than the contemporary anchors.

saves.album_name: Me Chama De Gato Que Eu Sou Sua
saves.reason: Follow the Brazilian thread in Hannah Cohen and V.V. Lightbody into contemporary MPB: bossa-funk, woozy synths, warm horns, dreamy vocal layers and lush soul/orchestral arrangements. Try Insista em Mim for warmth, then Electric Fish for disco-funk movement. Bolder and more dancefloor-forward: a neighbouring branch, not an exact replica.

The percussion/bass-first branch of the V.V. Lightbody / Hannah Cohen lane: Latin rhythms, supple bass, sparkling keyboards, airy vocals and woozy psychedelic lounge-pop. Try Day Dreaming, then Softened Thoughts. More electronic/dance-led and less lyrically foregrounded. New album in the checked history, not a completely new artist: one prior Ooo La La (bad tuner Remix) scrobble.

Recent-release discovery after V.V. Lightbody’s Period Piece and Hannah Cohen’s Earthstar Mountain. Strong orchestral/Brazilian match: soft lead vocals, female backing harmonies, flute, strings, electric piano, warm bass and understated percussion. Fuller and closer to Cohen’s lush arrangements than Grandeza. Try Dodói, then Nome de Deus; Roupa Dos Mortos for instrumental flute. Portuguese-language singing; saved despite the preference for English lyrics because the instrumental fit is strong.

Especially close to Practice Smiling: airy English vocals, electric piano, flute, Brazilian funk/samba and city-pop movement, with anxiety and dark lyrics beneath cheerful music. Jonathan Rado’s full-band production is earthier and more song-forward than Coast 2 Coast. Try Stratford & 52 and Doom Mood; Wide Awake for tenderness and shared vulnerability. One of the strongest English-language choices in this lane.

Newer continuation of the Dina Ögon / Hannah Cohen groove connection: warm sophisticated soul-pop, honeyed guitar, delicate drums, jazzy harmonies and Minnie Riperton-like melodies, with a more melancholy atmosphere than Oas. Try Grå labyrint, then Dålig teve. Longer, polished double LP with Swedish vocals; a harmony/rhythm-section match rather than primarily a flute match. Reviews disagree on the lyrical quality.

The warm, lyrics-engaging branch of the Period Piece / Earthstar Mountain lane: intimate vocal arrangements, substantial bass, light percussion, horns and touches of woodwind, blending calypso, jazz and bossa nova. Mostly English with a French closer; relationship writing and political themes beneath sweet musical surfaces. Try Something You Said, Summer Meadows and TIEF. Less psychedelic than the anchors, but strong warmth and rhythmic lightness.

The quieter pastoral Hannah Cohen branch: Brazilian-rooted orchestral psych-folk, acoustic guitar, lush strings, harmonized singing, subtle percussion and cinematic interludes. Try Feel for jazzy rhythmic movement, then Conclusão for tenderness; Lighthouse for an English-language song. Primarily Portuguese and more diffuse than Practice Smiling; saved for the arrangement/atmosphere connection despite the usual preference for English lyrics.

Follow Laure Briard’s earlier recommendation into her 2026 album: French yé-yé, Californian psych-folk, reflective soft rock and bittersweet introspection. Try Rocking Chair, then Force Invisible. More folky and less directly Brazilian/groove-oriented than Ne pas trop rester bleue. Mixed French/English singing; saved for the musical fit despite the general preference for English lyrics.

English-language, lyrics-first neighbour to Practice Smiling: Jane Penny’s breathy vocals and flute, melodic bass, shimmering synths and disco movement carry longing, troubled relationships and disillusionment. Try Outstanding in the Rain and Your Ride for the instrumental match, then Chlorine for the emotional writing. More 1980s city-pop/synth-pop than Brazilian folk. Familiar artist but no album plays in the checked history; reviews differ on whether its consistency becomes sameness.

Already in the Qobuz library when this pass was researched, but no matching scrobbles: a reminder to listen, not a new library discovery. Strong neighbouring match to V.V. Lightbody and Hannah Cohen: lush Brazilian-German MPB, samba, psychedelic disco, strings, vintage synths and warm analog/live-ensemble production. Themes of migration, belonging and relationships. Try Bem Querer, then Mar sem Dar Pé. Portuguese singing and more dance-oriented; saved with notes despite the general preference for English lyrics.
